formats.description: Where the additive can be classified into a Schedule 7 class, use the class name followed by the Schedule 8 name or code number; where multiple classes fit, use the most appropriate class.
Where the additive cannot be classified into a Schedule 7 class, use its Schedule 8 name.
An enzyme may be declared as enzyme without its specific name.
A flavouring substance may be declared as flavouring, flavour, or by a more specific name or description.
Specified glutamate and nucleotide substances added as flavouring substances or flavouring ingredients must be specifically declared in accordance with subsection (1).
Added caffeine, whether as a flavouring or otherwise, is to be listed as caffeine.

governingProvisions.effect: A food additive requires Schedule 15 permission and compliance with its applicable restrictions; GMP use is limited to the amount necessary under GMP.
Carry-over is conditional and is not available for infant formula products; product classification and carry-over evidence remain unresolved.
Apply the applicable Schedule 15 permission and limit for the relevant additive or colouring type.
Combined maximum-level colourings are subject to 70 mg/L in beverages or 290 mg/kg in other foods; applicability is not evaluated in this turn.
Unless otherwise specified, apply a limit to food prepared as directed; an ingredient limit may differ where the final food meets the applicable limit.
Use the specified calculation bases and steviol-equivalent factors only where a mapped candidate row applies.
Restrict intense-sweetener use to the permitted purposes unless Schedule 15 expressly provides otherwise; one child-row exception is transcribed separately.
Where additives share a technological purpose, their concentration-to-limit proportions may be aggregated; GMP substances are excluded from that calculation.
A class receives direct rows and rows under higher-level headings; sibling and lower-level heading rows do not inherit.
Additives in a preparation require permission under category 0; category 0 is not a general finished-food permission.
Maximum levels default to mg/kg unless indicated otherwise; GMP means the maximum level necessary for the technological purpose under GMP.
The additive-type headings refer to the relevant Schedule 16 lists; named row membership is not inferred here.
A formulated caffeinated beverage is a water-based flavoured drink for Schedule 15 item 14.1.3; apply other subclasses only when separately established.
The separate 145–320 mg/L total-caffeine requirement is not the Schedule 15 cola-type-drink caffeine row.

reviewNotes: Schedule 15 S15—2 inheritance was checked: no permission rows occur directly under heading 13, 14 or 14.1 and flow into the candidate classes. The 13.1 and 14.1 child rows are not inherited into 13.2 or 14.1.3; inheritedPermissionRowIds are intentionally empty.

The Standard 2.6.4 link to 14.1.3 is explicit for formulated caffeinated beverages. The separate Schedule 15 child categories remain candidate-only and require product facts. Foods for infants item 13.2 remains candidate-only; do not extend it to infant formula products or infer category from marketing.

The three S15 type headings at 14.1.3 refer to Schedule 16 S16—2, S16—3 and S16—4. Their list memberships are not transcribed here, so type grants are broad candidates and this is not a complete permission set. No individual S15 row is mapped to a Schedule 16 list.

Schedule 14 S14—2 purpose vocabulary is recorded separately. It does not map a particular additive or Schedule 15 row to a technological purpose; the app must not infer purpose from a substance name or INS identifier.
Schedule 15 identifiers are preserved as printed and are not mapped to Schedule 8 names or codes. No Schedule 7 class mapping or additive identity crosswalk is asserted.

The Schedule 15 item 13.2 row for INS 414 Gum arabic has an apparent printed maximum level of 10, but table presentation requires verification against the registered source. It remains explicitly unverified and draft.
Five modified-starch rows in item 13.2 share the printed condition "In total"; their shared aggregation group prevents treating each maximum as independent.

Standard 1.3.1 Amendment 231 has a transition concerning specified infant-formula changes through 2029-09-13. It is not a general transition for item 13.2. Any infant-formula classification or transition requires separate review.

All category, type, limit, condition, purpose, calculation-basis and governing-provision data are draft candidates. This catalog performs no permission, mixture, concentration, exemption, classification or compliance evaluation.
